articles.title: UNDRR Concept Note: World Tsunami Awareness Day 2026
articles.description: Please refer to the attached file. The theme of World Tsunami Awareness Day 2026, on 5 November, is “Be Tsunami Ready: Resilience Starts With You”. It builds on WTAD 2025’s emphasis on investment in preparedness by focusing on individual and community action. The theme supports global messaging on recognising natural tsunami warning signs, moving immediately to high ground or inland when needed, knowing local evacuation routes, preparing household emergency plans, taking part in community drills, and helping people who may require additional support, including children, older persons, persons with disabilities and tourists. The theme aligns with the final stretch of Sendai Framework implementation to 2030, with the Early Warnings for All initiative, and with the continued expansion of the UNESCO-IOC Tsunami Ready Programme. Calls for Action We call on national and local governments, civil protection agencies and disaster management authorities to organise or support tsunami evacuation drills and #GetToHighGround activities during the week of 5 November. We call on schools, universities and educators to integrate tsunami awareness into curricula, run age-appropriate drills and support youth-led preparedness campaigns. We call on municipalities, tourism operators, hotels and workplaces in coastal areas to familiarise staff and visitors with evacuation routes and natural warning signs. We call on media organisations and content creators to help translate tsunami risk knowledge into clear, accessible and locally relevant messaging. We call on organisations representing persons with disabilities, older persons and migrants to help shape inclusive preparedness materials and activities.

articles.title: Union Demands Safety Overhaul After Ammonia Leaks at Costa Rican Ice Cream Plant
articles.description: Two ammonia leaks occurred at the Dos Pinos ice cream plant in the coastal district of Coyola, Alajuela, on Sunday, October 25, and Monday, October 26. The union representing the workers, Union de Empleados de la Cooperativa Dos Pinos (Udeco), reported that four employees required emergency medical attention: three women who felt ill during evacuation and a mechanic who sustained a hand burn. Udeco stated that the first incident began around 9:00 a. m. on Sunday during maintenance of equipment unit number 304. The union claimed that emergency response personnel were absent from the area, forcing staff to manage the evacuation themselves. The second incident occurred around 10:20 a. m. on Monday, following the rupture of a valve during technical intervention. According to the union, the mechanic was working without personal protective equipment, which resulted in an ammonia cloud forming in the production zone. A central issue in the union's complaint is the absence of dedicated ammonia detection systems. Udeco noted that while the facility is equipped with standard smoke detectors and fire alarms, it lacks devices that specifically detect gas refrigerant leaks. The union also cited blocked evacuation routes, claiming one exit was locked and another obstructed by stacked pallets and cargo. Witness accounts collected by Udeco indicate that some staff had to use alternative routes to leave the danger zone, and one worker was temporarily trapped while attempting to exit through a service door.
